arxiv-2111-02717.title: Facial Emotion Recognition using Deep Residual Networks in Real-World Environments
arxiv-2111-02717.creator: Panagiotis Tzirakis, Dénes Boros, Elnar Hajiyev, Björn W. Schuller
arxiv-2111-02717.description: Abstract Automatic affect recognition using visual cues is an important task towards a complete interaction between humans and machines. Applications can be found in tutoring systems and human computer interaction. A critical step towards that direction is facial feature extraction.

arxiv-2206-02549.title: Mathematical Operations and Equation Solving with Reconfigurable Metadevices
arxiv-2206-02549.creator: Dimitrios C. Tzarouchis, Mario Junior Mencagli, Brian Edwards, Nader Engheta
arxiv-2206-02549.description: Abstract Performing analog computations with metastructures is an emerging wave-based paradigm for solving mathematical problems. For such devices, one major challenge is their reconfigurability, especially without the need for a priori mathematical computations or computationally-intensive optimization. Their equation-solving capabilities are applied only to matrices with special spectral (eigenvalue) distribution.

arxiv-2211-04442.title: Algorithmic bias in machine learning based delirium prediction
arxiv-2211-04442.creator: Sandhya Tripathi, Bradley A Fritz, Michael S Avidan, Yixin Chen, Christopher R King
arxiv-2211-04442.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sandhya Tripathi, Bradley A Fritz, Michael S Avidan, Yixin Chen, Christopher R King. Although prediction models for delirium, a commonly occurring condition during general hospitalization or post-surgery, have not gained huge popularity, their algorithmic bias evaluation is crucial due to the existing association between social determinants of health and delirium risk. In this context, using MIMIC-III and another academic hospital dataset, we present some initial experimental evidence showing how sociodemographic features such as sex and race can impact the model performance across subgroups.

arxiv-2212-05240.title: Protocol selection for second-order consensus against disturbance Note: This work was supported in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant 62273267; in part by the Natural Science Basic Research Program of Shaanxi under Grant 2022JC-46.
arxiv-2212-05240.creator: Jiamin Wang, Liqi Zhou, Dong Zhang, Jian Liu, Yuanshi Zheng
arxiv-2212-05240.description: Abstract Noticing that both the absolute and relative velocity protocols can solve the second-order consensus of multi-agent systems, this paper aims to investigate which of the above two protocols has better anti-disturbance capability, in which the anti-disturbance capability is measured by the ℒ 2 {\mathcal{L}}_{2}\ gain from the disturbance to the consensus error.

arxiv-2305-01780.title: Synchronization of silicon thermal free-carrier oscillators
arxiv-2305-01780.creator: Gustavo de O. Luiz, Caique C. Rodrigues, Thiago P. M. Alegre, Gustavo S. Wiederhecker
arxiv-2305-01780.description: Abstract Recent exploration of collective phenomena in oscillator arrays has highlighted its potential for accessing a range of physical phenomena, from fundamental quantum many-body dynamics Heinrich et al. 2011 to the solution of practical optimization problems using photonic Ising machines Marandi et al. 2014 ; Wang et al. 2013 .

arxiv-2309-10078.title: Simple and Optimal Online Contention Resolution Schemes for k k -Uniform Matroids
arxiv-2309-10078.creator: Atanas Dinev, S. Matthew Weinberg
arxiv-2309-10078.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Atanas Dinev, S. Matthew Weinberg. We provide a simple ( 1 − O ⁡ ( 1 k ) ) (1-O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}})) -selectable Online Contention Resolution Scheme for k k -uniform matroids against a fixed-order adversary.

arxiv-2311-01718.title: A high-performance surface acoustic wave sensing technique
arxiv-2311-01718.creator: Mengmeng Wu, Xiao Liu, Renfei Wang, Xi Lin, Yang Liu
arxiv-2311-01718.description: Abstract We present a superheterodyne-scheme demodulation system which can detect the amplitude and phaseshift of weak radio-frequency signals with extraordinarily high stability and resolution. As a demonstration, we introduce a process to measure the velocity of the surface acoustic wave using a delay-line device from 30 K to room temperature, which can resolve < \textless 0.1ppm velocity shift.

arxiv-2401-02650.title: Improving sample efficiency of high dimensional Bayesian optimization with MCMC
arxiv-2401-02650.creator: Zeji Yi, Yunyue Wei, Chu Xin Cheng, Kaibo He, Yanan Sui
arxiv-2401-02650.description: Abstract Sequential optimization methods are often confronted with the curse of dimensionality in high-dimensional spaces. Current approaches under the Gaussian process framework are still burdened by the computational complexity of tracking Gaussian process posteriors and need to partition the optimization problem into small regions to ensure exploration or assume an underlying low-dimensional structure.

arxiv-2504-08775.title: Layers at Similar Depths Generate Similar Activations Across LLM Architectures
arxiv-2504-08775.creator: Christopher Wolfram, Aaron Schein
arxiv-2504-08775.description: Abstract How do the latent spaces used by independently-trained LLMs relate to one another? We study the nearest neighbor relationships induced by activations at different layers of 24 open-weight LLMs, and find that they 1) tend to vary from layer to layer within a model, and 2) are approximately shared between corresponding layers of different models.

arxiv-2509-12948.title: A Learnable Fully Interacted Two-Tower Model for Pre-Ranking System DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation email; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 Conference: Proceedings of the 48th International
arxiv-2509-12948.creator: Chao Xiong, Xianwen Yu, Wei Xu, Lei Cheng, Chuan Yuan, Linjian Mo
arxiv-2509-12948.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chao Xiong, Xianwen Yu, Wei Xu, Lei Cheng, Chuan Yuan, Linjian Mo. Pre-ranking plays a crucial role in large-scale recommender systems by significantly improving the efficiency and scalability within the constraints of providing high-quality candidate sets in real time. The two-tower model is widely used in pre-ranking systems due to a good balance between efficiency and effectiveness with decoupled architecture, which independently processes user and item inputs before calculating their interaction (e.g. dot product or similarity measure).

arxiv-2509-23294.title: Programmable Focal Elongation and Shaping of High-Intensity Laser Pulses using Adaptive Optics Journal: opticajournal
arxiv-2509-23294.creator: Peter Blum, Anna Puchert, Emily Archer, Sören Jalas, Spencer W. Jolly, Jens Osterhoff, Wim P. Leemans, Manuel Kirchen, Andreas R. Maier, Rob J. Shalloo
arxiv-2509-23294.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Peter Blum, Anna Puchert, Emily Archer, Sören Jalas, Spencer W. Jolly, Jens Osterhoff, Wim P. Leemans, Manuel Kirchen, Andreas R. Maier, Rob J. Shalloo. Controlling the intensity distribution of laser pulses in the focal region is essential for optimizing optically generated plasma waveguides and enabling advanced plasma acceleration techniques, including dephasingless wakefield acceleration.

arxiv-2510-08219.title: Post-hoc Stochastic Concept Bottleneck Models
arxiv-2510-08219.creator: Wiktor Jan Hoffmann, Sonia Laguna, Moritz Vandenhirtz, Emanuele Palumbo, Julia E. Vogt
arxiv-2510-08219.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wiktor Jan Hoffmann, Sonia Laguna, Moritz Vandenhirtz, Emanuele Palumbo, Julia E. Vogt. Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) are interpretable models that predict the target variable through high-level human-understandable concepts, allowing users to intervene on mispredicted concepts to adjust the final output. While recent work has shown that modeling dependencies between concepts can improve CBM performance, especially under interventions, such approaches typically require retraining the entire model, which may be infeasible when access to the original data or compute is limited.

arxiv-2601-23183.title: JobResQA: A Benchmark for LLM Machine Reading Comprehension on Multilingual Résumés and JDs
arxiv-2601-23183.creator: Casimiro Pio Carrino, Paula Estrella, Rabih Zbib, Carlos Escolano, José A. R. Fonollosa
arxiv-2601-23183.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Casimiro Pio Carrino, Paula Estrella, Rabih Zbib, Carlos Escolano, José A. R. Fonollosa. We introduce JobResQA, a multilingual Question Answering benchmark for evaluating Machine Reading Comprehension (MRC) capabilities of LLMs on HR-specific tasks involving résumés and job descriptions. The dataset comprises 581 QA pairs across 105 synthetic résumé-job description pairs in five languages (English, Spanish, Italian, German, and Chinese), with questions spanning three complexity levels from basic factual extraction to complex cross-document reasoning.

pmc-12400466.title: Effect of early micro-breastfeeding on growth rate and postpartum depression in preterm infants with low-birth-weight
pmc-12400466.creator: Yu Chen, Sheng-Lan Cai
pmc-12400466.description: BACKGROUNDPremature infant formula is based on milk and contains energy, vitamins, etc. Breast milk is rich in minerals, such as phosphorus and calcium, and proteins. Both can be used for nutritional support in preterm infants with low-birth-weight. However, their effects on the difference in infant growth rate and postpartum depression are still unclear.

pmc-12625061.title: Outpatient healthcare costs of childhood injuries in Australia: a 15-year longitudinal analysis using linked survey and health insurance data
pmc-12625061.creator: Aquib M. Chowdhury, Kabir Ahmad, Rasheda Khanam
pmc-12625061.description: ObjectiveThis study evaluated the excess out-of-hospital healthcare costs associated with unintentional childhood injuries in Australia. This relationship was investigated within a longitudinal biennially surveyed cohort of 8,852 children aged 0–19 years. We assessed whether costs increased over age and with the duration of injury prevalence. Results were compared against cost estimates from similar studies in Australia and analogous developed nations.

pmc-12648976.title: Validation of Shona Symptom Questionnaire (SSQ-14), Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) and Generalised Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7) in Unguja Island, Zanzibar
pmc-12648976.creator: Diana Ceccolini, Jermaine Dambi, Haji Fatawi, Suleiman Ali, Simon Kühnert, Lindsay Solera-Deuchar, Jabir James, Catherine Odhiambo, Peter McGovern, Whitney Taiwo, Ruth Verhey, Dixon Chibanda
pmc-12648976.description: BackgroundDue to the dearth of resources in low- and middle-income countries, the use of culturally appropriate and psychometrically robust screening tools for common mental disorders (CMDs) administrable by lay health workers (LHWs) is critical to both identifying people that need care and collecting prevalence data to inform policy decisions.

pmc-12686592.title: Defining Microbiota‐Derived Metabolite Butyrate as a Senomorphic: Therapeutic Potential in the Age‐Related T Cell Senescence
pmc-12686592.creator: Nia Paddison Rees, Jessica Conway, Ben Dugan, Sayeda S. Amir, Aimee Parker, Simon R. Carding, Niharika A. Duggal
pmc-12686592.description: Advancing age is accompanied by an accumulation of senescent T cells that secrete pro‐inflammatory senescence‐associated secretory phenotype (SASP) molecules. Gut‐microbiota‐derived signals are increasingly recognised as immunomodulators. In the current study, we demonstrated that ageing and the accumulation of senescent T cells are accompanied by a reduction in microbial‐derived short‐chain fatty acids (SCFAs).

pmc-12968250.title: The evaluation of the plasma levels of interleukin 17A, thymic stromal lymphopoietin, interferon gamma, tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interleukins IL-2, IL-6, IL-23, and IL-31 in atopic dermatitis patients with dupilumab treatment
pmc-12968250.creator: Jarmila Čelakovská, Eva Čermáková, Petra Boudkova, Ctirad Andrýs
pmc-12968250.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundInterleukin -17 (IL-17), particularly IL-17A, thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP), interferon gamma (IFN-γ), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), IL-2, IL-6, IL-23, and IL-31 play a significant role in the pathogenesis of various chronic inflammatory and autoimmune skin diseases.MethodWe conducted an assessment of plasma levels of interleukins IL-17A, TSLP, IFN-γ TNF-α, IL-2, IL-6, IL-23, and IL-31 in 89 atopic dermatitis (AD) patients and in 34 healthy individuals as a control group.

pmc-12997533.title: Miniaturisation of Raman spectroscopy systems: from benchtop to backpocket
pmc-12997533.creator: Mike Hardy, Pooja P. Kanade, Emma Buchan, Pola Goldberg Oppenheimer, Cillian P. T. McPolin, Robert M. Bowman
pmc-12997533.description: The global portable spectroscopy market is rapidly expanding, with optical technologies composing the greatest market share. One prominent light-based technology is Raman spectroscopy, which confers benefits in terms of high selectivity and thus untargeted detection and multiplexing capabilities. Alongside this, plasmon-enhanced Raman technologies can provide ultra-low, even single molecule, detection.

pmc-13182141.title: Shoulder-to-shoulder: healthcare professionals’ experiences of learning during electronic health record implementation in municipal primary care
pmc-13182141.creator: Christin Uvsløkk Wiggen, Kirsti Sarheim Anthun, Erna Håland, Monica Lillefjell
pmc-13182141.description: BackgroundFormal training is commonly used in electronic health record (EHR) implementation, but often fails to address healthcare professionals’ ongoing, context-specific learning needs. There is limited knowledge of how learning unfolds in practice when such training is experienced as insufficient, particularly in municipal healthcare services.

pmc-13234127.title: Optimization of protein extraction from skin tape strips for biomarker assessment
pmc-13234127.creator: Tiana Stanisic, Caroline Meyer Olesen, Maria Oberländer Christensen, Beatrice Dyring-Andersen, Marianne Bengtson Løvendorf, Jop Vreeken, Florentine de Boer, Sanja Kezic, Martin Kongsbak-Wismann
pmc-13234127.description: Stratum corneum tape-stripping is a non-invasive alternative to biopsies for biomarker analysis in inflammatory skin diseases, but low-abundance protein detection is challenging. High extraction yield is therefore crucial, yet extraction protocols vary. Because total protein collected on the tapes is commonly used for biomarker normalization, factors influencing its measurement can impact data interpretation.
